submissions.findingTextShort: A 12-week randomized trial of standardized Salacia reticulata extract found a modest reduction in DXA total fat mass, but the second coprimary body-fat-percentage endpoint was null, so the clinical evidence remains preliminary.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: PMID 42187323 reports a 12-week randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of a standardized Salacia reticulata extract in adults with overweight and/or obesity. The modified intention-to-treat analysis included 66 extract and 67 placebo participants. Total body fat mass favored the extract by an adjusted between-group difference of -482.30 g (95% CI -907.05 to -57.54; P=.0158), while body-fat percentage did not differ significantly (-0.30 percentage points, 95% CI -0.73 to 0.12; P=.1453). Several secondary regional fat measures were directionally favorable. The authors characterize the mixed coprimary findings as preliminary and note retrospective trial registration. This source supports only a modest, formulation-specific body-composition signal over 12 weeks and must not be converted into a generic weight-loss or obesity-treatment claim.
submissions.populationContext: Adults with overweight and/or obesity; 66 standardized-extract and 67 placebo participants in the modified intention-to-treat analysis.
submissions.usageContext: Exact standardized Salacia reticulata extract only. Preserve 12-week duration, DXA measurement, overweight/obesity population, and the distinction between total fat mass and the null body-fat-percentage coprimary endpoint.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Mixed coprimary findings and retrospective registration materially limit inference. Do not generalize to other Salacia species, leaves/root-bark preparations, biscuits, combination products, or acute glycemic studies. Studied dosing is not consumer-dose guidance. The trial's author list includes R&D staff of Daehan Chemtech Co., Ltd. and RnBS Corp.; this industry sponsorship must remain attached to the finding.
